title: A Blueprint for Auditing Generative AI
venue: Research Handbook of the Law of Artificial Intelligence (book chapter preprint; based on AI and Ethics article)
extended_summary:
This chapter addresses the question of how generative AI systems should be audited in order to identify and manage ethical, legal, and technical risks. The authors argue that existing auditing procedures are too narrow for generative AI because these systems are adaptable across many downstream tasks and can display emergent capabilities, making it difficult to rely on a single audit point or a single standard set of checks.

The paper proposes a three-layer auditing blueprint. At the governance level, providers of generative AI systems should undergo audits of organizational procedures, accountability structures, and quality management systems. At the model level, pre-trained systems should be audited for technical characteristics such as performance, information security, and robustness. At the application level, downstream products and services built on generative AI should undergo continuous audits of functionality and impact, with attention to legality, ethical alignment, and real-world effects over time.

The chapter is conceptual rather than empirical and does not study a school or education setting. Its target audience is technology providers, policymakers, and independent auditors. The main conclusion is that effective oversight of generative AI requires coordinated governance, model, and application audits, ideally conducted by independent third parties with appropriate levels of access. The authors also emphasize that auditing can improve transparency and accountability, but it cannot by itself eliminate all harms or resolve all normative disagreements about fairness, privacy, and acceptable use.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI systems that can produce content such as text, images, audio, or code, including large language models and other foundation-model-based applications.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper does not evaluate a specific classroom product; it proposes a governance and auditing blueprint for generative AI systems and their downstream applications in general.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/legal policy chapter proposing an auditing blueprint, not an empirical evaluation of an AI tool in educational settings. There is no study design, sample, or measured outcome to assess.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational intervention or outcome was tested, so there is no empirical impact to judge. The paper discusses governance mechanisms rather than student or teacher effects.
